prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2010 manifesto sets out a progressive, reforming programme for a “future fair for all,” rejecting a return to business as usual after the financial crisis and the expenses scandal. It argues for active government that backs ordinary people, protects frontline services, and rebuilds trust, while confronting global competition, climate change, ageing, and security challenges with judgement and optimism—not the Conservatives’ pessimism, early cuts, and tilt to the privileged few.

Economy and jobs: Labour will secure the recovery—no reckless cuts in 2010—and more than halve the deficit by 2014 through growth, fair taxes and targeted savings, with those with the “broadest shoulders” paying most (50p top rate, bonus tax, NI rise next year, reduced pension tax relief for the best‑off). Banks face tighter regulation, higher capital, living wills and a global levy; more competition and mutuals are encouraged. A proactive industrial strategy will back high‑tech and green sectors, UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), a Green Investment Bank, High Speed Rail, universal broadband, a ring‑fenced science budget and modern infrastructure—supporting one million skilled jobs.

Work, welfare and living standards: Labour will end a life on benefits with job guarantees (Future Jobs Fund, mandatory offers at 6–24 months), ensure work pays (Minimum Wage rising at least with earnings; £40/week Better Off in Work guarantee), expand apprenticeships and Skills Accounts, and champion SMEs (rate relief, credit adjudicator). It helps households onto the housing ladder (stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers; clampdown on sub‑prime practices), expands affordable and council homes, and protects savers (People’s Bank at the Post Office; curb exploitative lending).

Public services: Frontline spending on childcare, schools, the NHS and policing is protected; reform empowers citizens. Education guarantees 1‑to‑1 tuition in the 3Rs, personal tutors, strong discipline, fair admissions, more early years support and parent “triggers” to change failing leadership; proven school groups, academies and co‑ops spread excellence. The NHS offers legal guarantees (18‑week treatment or funded private alternative; 1‑week cancer diagnostics), prevention (health checks 40–74; mental health access), more home care, GP choice and personal budgets—funded by efficiencies, not cuts to care.

Families, ageing and care: Labour backs all families, not just a few—Father’s Month, flexible leave, a Toddler Tax Credit, and an end to default retirement at 65 with a right to flexible work for older people. A National Care Service will deliver free home care for the highest needs and cap residential costs after two years; the State Pension re‑links to earnings in 2012 and personal pension saving is expanded.

Safer communities and fair migration: Police and PCSO numbers are maintained; neighbourhood teams stay visible; failing forces can be taken over. Fast, effective action tackles anti‑social behaviour, with a right to injunctions for repeat victims. Technology (CCTV/DNA) is used with safeguards. An Australian‑style points system controls immigration to meet economic needs; English and citizenship are strengthened and borders are enforced.

Green growth: Around 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 and 400,000 green jobs by 2015, with “pay‑as‑you‑save” home upgrades, smart meters, zero‑waste ambition, protected Green Belt, linked habitats, fairer food chains (Supermarkets Ombudsman), and rural broadband.

New politics: Clean up and open up—IPSA, recall for misconduct, a statutory lobbyists register, ban MPs’ lobbying jobs, fixed‑term Parliaments, referenda on AV and an elected second chamber, a free vote on votes at 16, stronger local government scrutiny, and open data for real accountability.

Global role and security: Support our forces and veterans; a Strategic Defence Review while maintaining the nuclear deterrent and pursuing multilateral disarmament. A clear strategy in Afghanistan, robust counter‑terrorism, leadership in an outward‑facing EU, UN/IFIs reform, and 0.7% aid in law. This is not a conservative moment—it is a progressive one.
